Having taught CCW classes, I'm split between weeding out the Completely incompetent who will absolutely do unintentional harm to themselves or another and having no barrier to exercising Constitutional rights.

Classes shouldn't be Mandatory, but I sure wish there were a TON more social pressure to take them. The time spent on law alone was worth the paltry fee. We've always had the county DA (a gun nut himself) come in for the night and talk about the laws. But hands-on practical, for people who had NEVER fired a gun before (easily half the class, every class) was every bit as important. Hell, I wish there were social pressure within the shooting community to take refresher classes, be active in some sort of practical competitions (IDPA/IPSC come to mind), and just generally work on continuing competency. With both a mother and a wife working in the medical field, I hear of way too may cases of "accidental discharge" due to inept users.

So, I'm torn when I see this news. I know the level of dumbassery that exists and wish there were a way to adjust that a little Before they carry a weapon in person. Much like you have to pass a basic competency test before driving a weapon in public.

Not to mention open carry can also just make you a target...I mean I agree with open carry laws. But really I just think the classes should be subsidized and the fees for submitting your paperwork should be about half of what they are now.
